strengths: Novel geometry-grounded BPE analog for protein structures, addressing key limitations of VQ-VAE-based tokenizers (fixed codebook, poor interpretability, fixed token size)
Exceptional out-of-distribution generalization (test/train RMSD ratio 1.16-1.28 vs. 6.4× for VQ-VAE), demonstrating robustness to unseen structural variability
Comprehensive evaluation across 10 research questions on 12 downstream tasks (24 splits) with systematic investigation of compression, distortion, generalization, efficiency, and interpretability
Tokens align with CATH functional families (F1=0.996, IOU=0.992) and functional domains, providing semantic meaning absent in prior PSTs, validated through expert case studies
Strong downstream transfer performance with +15.44% improvement on functional site prediction and +43.28% on structure property prediction, and exceptional data efficiency (1% pretraining data)
Rigorous technical formulation with principled alternating local-global optimization (k-medoids clustering + differentiable inverse kinematics under SE(3) constraints)
Excellent reproducibility with 23 detailed algorithms, hyperparameter specifications, computational complexity analysis, and promised code release
weaknesses: Uneven task-specific performance with significant degradation on some tasks (Rep fold: −24.44%, FlexRMSF fold: −8.17%), weakening claims of broad superiority

Confounded downstream comparison: VQ-VAE features jointly learned while GEOBPE uses pretrained ESM3 features, conflating tokenizer quality with feature extractor quality and reducing fairness of comparison
Limited and preliminary generative capabilities: SSLM-Eval on only 100 samples acknowledged as 'proof of concept', with VQ-VAE showing higher diversity (58% vs. 49%)
Scalability concerns: tested only to 21K tokens, extensive hand-tuned hyperparameters (Mmax=5000, P=10) with different settings per experiment (Appendix I) raise generalization questions
Data efficiency claims oversold: Table 3 shows GEOBPE (1%) sometimes underperforms full model (PhysChem 44.50% vs. 45.26%), contradicting 'no meaningful drop' claims
Missing key ablations and design justifications: no comparison of k-medoids to alternatives, limited analysis of IK loss function choice, ablation of core components beyond glue optimization
Downstream feature dependency: V-induced representations require pretrained ESM3, not a self-contained solution, limiting modularity claims
Limited expert evaluation: only 3 proteins for case studies, CATH FunFams validation uses sequence-derived HMM annotations (not independent structural ground truth), somewhat circular validation

strengths: Novel geometry-grounded BPE formulation for protein backbones with principled handling of SE(3) constraints and drift correction via differentiable IK

Exceptionally thorough experimental evaluation: 10 research questions, 12 downstream tasks across 24 splits, extensive ablations, strong OOD generalization (1.16-1.28× test/train RMSD vs. 6.4× for VQ-VAE)

Superior interpretability compared to VQ-VAEs: tokens are explicit geometric medoids from observed structures, align with CATH domains (99.97% recall), supported by expert case studies showing functional relevance
Strong empirical results on core compression tasks: 0.27-0.36× BPR of ProToken with comparable distortion, data efficiency at 1% pretraining data, consistent downstream improvements (+15.44% average)
Excellent reproducibility: 25+ detailed algorithms, comprehensive hyperparameter guidelines, computational complexity analysis, promised code release
Architecture-agnostic design with hierarchical vocabulary providing multi-scale inductive bias for representation learning across multiple scales
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: tokenizes backbone atoms only, excludes sequence and side chains which are critical for real protein function; side chain integration remains speculative

Generative results underperform claims: only 4% designability at 7.3M params, 20.8% at 65.9M params—below ProtDiff (11.8%) and below state-of-the-art, authors explicitly state results 'not competitive with SOTA'

Downstream transfer improvements are confounded by ESM3 features: unclear how much gain comes from GEOBPE vocabulary vs. ESM3 embeddings; continuous PSTs often outperform in Table 1 (e.g., 75.92% vs 72.43%)

Prohibitive implementation complexity: 25+ algorithms, multiple interdependent hyperparameters (num_p, bins, glue_opt_every, etc.), high barrier to entry; heuristic guidelines for hyperparameter selection
Substantial computational cost: 200 CPU-days to tokenize 550K structures; periodic glue optimization is rate-limiting; scalability to billion-protein databases questionable
Incomplete justification of design choices: why medoids over learnable prototypes? How much of hierarchy benefit comes from structure vs. vocabulary quality? SE(3) loss may be overly restrictive

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across compression, OOD generalization, downstream tasks, and interpretability with extensive ablations
Genuine interpretability advances: tokens align with biological structures (CATH domains, functional sites) unlike VQ-VAEs
Strong out-of-distribution generalization (test/train RMSD 1.16-1.28 vs 6.4× for VQ-VAE)
Well-motivated problem identifying real limitations of VQ-VAE tokenizers
Multi-resolution capability through hierarchical vocabularies
Strong reproducibility commitment with detailed algorithms, hyperparameter documentation, and promised code
weaknesses: Unfair experimental comparisons: GEOBPE uses ~7% training data of baselines; downstream transfer uses ESM3 features while comparing against methods that jointly train features and tokens
Overstated claims about backbone generation: SSLM-Eval achieves only 4% designability even with 10× data/parameters, contradicting 'foundation model' positioning
Conceptual design flaw: geometric drift requiring iterative IK refinement suggests core quantization is fundamentally limited; the pipeline complexity (Algorithm 12) masks underlying issues
Limited novelty: combines well-established techniques (structural alphabets, k-medoids, inverse kinematics) without algorithmic innovations or theoretical insights
Mixed downstream results: GEOBPE-TRANSFER underperforms on several tasks (Rep, FlexBFactor); gains are selective rather than universal
Methodological concerns: K-medoids minimizes RMSD without justification this maximizes task relevance; greedy BPE-style merging may not produce optimal hierarchies
Significant fold-type variance: 30% performance degradation on certain fold classes with no explanation for generalization failures
Questionable principles formulation: Principles 1-3 defined post-hoc after method design rather than derived from first principles
Presentation density: 48 pages with key results scattered in appendix; distinction between GEOBPE variants confusing; heavy notation in main text

strengths: Novel geometry-grounded extension of BPE to protein backbones with clear motivation addressing VQ-VAE limitations
Sound technical execution: elegant alternating local-global decomposition with differentiable IK for drift correction
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 10 research questions with extensive ablations and multiple test sets
Strong empirical results: 0.27-0.36× BPR of ProToken, test/train RMSD ratio 1.16-1.28 (vs 6.4× for VQ-VAE), data efficiency with 1% training data
Interpretability demonstration: 99.97% domain recall on CATH, expert-validated functional motif discovery aligned with biological principles
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameter documentation (Appendix K), promised code release
Strong downstream transfer: consistent +15-43% improvement across 12 tasks with 24 test splits
weaknesses: Large-scale LM applications remain preliminary: scTM 0.405, 21% designability even with 10× scaling (far below production backbone design models)
Incomplete multimodal integration: only backbone geometry tokenized, sequence and side chains excluded despite multimodal motivation
Method complexity with many hyperparameters (num_p, bins, glue_opt_every, wR, wt) and 8-page tuning guidance; computational cost (~1 hour for 300 steps) may limit adoption
Unclear isolated contribution of hierarchical representation: missing direct ablation comparing hierarchical vs non-hierarchical variants
Theoretical-algorithmic gap: design choices (why k-medoids? why these IK weights?) and glue optimization formulation appear somewhat ad-hoc
Baseline tuning details: VQ-VAE configurations not explicitly discussed; unclear if GEOBPE hyperparameters received more thorough optimization
Limited failure analysis: brief discussion of poor performance on small folds (30% worse RMSD); no detailed characterization of when method struggles
Token efficiency paradox underexplored: VQ-VAE's 'less efficient' tokens generated 58% more diverse structures, contradicting uniform token usage intuition
